rules.name: UPX-packed PE
rules.description: UPX section names plus the UPX! marker. UPX is also used by legitimate software, so this is only a weak hint.

rules.name: UPX-packed ELF
rules.description: UPX stub strings in an ELF image: the 'UPX!' marker and the 'This file is packed with the UPX' banner. Common on stripped Linux malware and on some legitimate tools.

strings.name: b
strings.value: packed with the UPX executable packer

rules.name: UPX-packed Mach-O
rules.description: UPX marker and banner inside a Mach-O image.

strings.name: b
strings.value: packed with the UPX executable packer

rules.name: Themida/WinLicense-style section names
rules.description: Section names .themida and .winlice are used by the Themida and WinLicense protectors (public packer documentation).

rules.name: VMProtect-style sections
rules.description: Sections named .vmp0 and .vmp1 left by the VMProtect virtualiser.

rules.name: PECompact-packed PE
rules.description: PEC2 / pec1 / pec2 markers used by PECompact.

rules.name: Petite or FSG-packed PE
rules.description: Petite's .petite section or the FSG! signature near the header.

rules.name: PyInstaller bundle
rules.description: PyInstaller cookie 'MEI' + magic and bootloader strings. Plenty of benign tools ship this way; it only tells the analyst to unpack the archive.

rules.name: Go binary with stripped build info and dense gibberish symbols
rules.description: Go runtime marker with the build-info header missing: typical of garble/strip-obfuscated Go implants (and some hardened vendor builds).
